claims.text: Powder-bed pre-heating during L-PBF of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi will lower thermal gradients.
Lower thermal gradients will reduce elemental segregation in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Lower thermal gradients will reduce residual stress in L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Powder-bed pre-heating will reduce defect formation and enhance the mechanical integrity of L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi.
A powder-bed pre-heating range of 200–400°C is suitable for the proposed intervention.
Laser power and scan speed are important process parameters for L-PBF high-entropy alloys.
The pre-heating temperature should remain below the recrystallization temperature of AlCrFeNiSi.
An elevated substrate temperature produces a more homogeneous AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Pre-heating slows the solidification cooling rate.
Slower cooling minimizes rapid temperature differentials responsible for compositional segregation and stress localization.
Reduced temperature differentials lead to fewer microcracks and hot cracks.
Pre-heated specimens will have lower segregation than non-preheated L-PBF specimens.
Pre-heated specimens will have lower residual stress and defect density than non-preheated L-PBF specimens.
Pre-heated specimens will exhibit improved tensile strength and ductility relative to non-preheated L-PBF specimens.
Conventional L-PBF AlCrFeNiSi exhibits pronounced thermal gradients that cause segregation, residual stress, and defects.
L-PBF process conditions can affect defect formation, microstructure, density, and mechanical performance in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed effect may not extend to substantially different energy inputs or other alloy systems.
The optimal pre-heating temperature and quantitative mechanical-property effects remain undetermined.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis initially uses the ambiguous comparator 'conventional processing,' whereas the predicted outcome and baseline define the comparator specifically as L-PBF without pre-heating. This leaves unclear whether the claimed advantage is over conventional bulk fabrication or over standard non-preheated L-PBF.
